title: Hengsheng Luthier Workshop
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Gu Heng（Gu Heng the luthier in his fifties, half-frame glasses, linen apron, sawdust on his cuffs, focused expression） enters the shavings workshop（Shavings workshop: wood scent everywhere, long bench with planes and calipers, golden shavings on the floor） and runs his hand over the spruce top plate（A spruce top plate with tight grain, surface planed mirror-smooth, join lines marked at the edges） on the bench.
Five vernier calipers（A row of five vernier calipers on the workshop tool board, metal gleaming） hang on the tool board; Gu Heng zeroes each one.
Two brass tuning forks（Two brass tuning forks hanging under the drying-gallery eaves, ringing at a light tap） hang under the drying-gallery eaves; Gu Heng taps them to let them ring.
Gu Heng circles the bench checking whether the plane irons are rolled.
Gu Heng gazes through the window at the fading string shadows in the instrument drying gallery.
Under the lamp the spruce top plate shows tight grain; Gu Heng feels the moisture with his fingertip.
Gu Heng sits on a wooden stool in the workshop corner for a brief rest.
Gu Heng opens the luthier notebook（A luthier notebook in cowhide cover, recording wood moisture and arch data） and records the day's top-plate arch.
Gu Heng draws a thickness-distribution curve in the luthier notebook.
Gu Heng closes the luthier notebook and puts it back in the bench chest.
The join lines at the spruce top plate edges are clear; Gu Heng nods.
Gu Heng wipes sawdust from the notebook cover with a dry cloth.

In the morning instrument drying gallery（Instrument drying gallery: glass-roofed corridor, half-finished bodies hanging, sunlight casting string shadows）, Gu Heng greets young A-Xian（Apprentice A-Xian at fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, gray cloth short jacket, bright stubborn eyes） arriving with the instrument cart（A wooden instrument cart, bed lined with velvet, rail stamped with a small 'Gu' mark）.
A-Xian steadies the cart and smooths the velvet lining flat again.
Gu Heng points to three soundpost blanks（Three soundpost blanks bound with red cord on the bench corner, wood pale cream） on the bench corner and teaches A-Xian to read the wood grain.
A-Xian crouches by a gallery post, curious about the hanging half-finished bodies.
Gu Heng explains the bass-bar line; A-Xian listens and nods seriously.
A-Xian looks back at the wooden instrument cart, eyes full of care.
Gu Heng has A-Xian practice measuring plate thickness with calipers first.

In the bustling instrument-street shopfront（Instrument-street shopfront: street-facing wooden counter, violins and bows on the wall, sign reading 'Hengsheng'）, A-Hui（Youth A-Hui, face very like A-Xian's, cream-white neck scarf, ebony hairpin at the temple, bold expression） in a cream-white neck scarf looks up from behind the counter.
A-Hui picks horsehair before the bow rack; her ebony hairpin sways slightly.
A-Hui haggles with a customer, expression bold.
A-Hui carries a violin case through the shopfront crowd.
A-Hui pauses under the 'Hengsheng' sign and looks back down the street.
On the instrument drying gallery, A-Xian and A-Hui stand side by side—one in indigo headscarf, one in cream-white neck scarf.
A-Xian hands soundpost blanks to A-Hui; the two compare the grain.
A-Hui straightens A-Xian's indigo headscarf; the two walk slowly along the gallery.
A-Xian and A-Hui part at the gallery end, one heading to the workshop and one to the shopfront.
A cross-breeze passes; their similar profiles cross and separate among the hanging bodies.
Months later at night, Gu Heng alone in the shavings workshop cooks fish glue.
Gu Heng opens the luthier notebook（The same luthier notebook soaked through with fish glue; cover sticky, ink blurred） and finds spilled fish glue has soaked the cover sticky.
Gu Heng wipes glue splashes from the spruce top plate.
Gu Heng looks out at the dark instrument drying gallery.
Under the lamp the spruce top plate glows pale gold; Gu Heng slowly runs his hand over the grain.
Gu Heng slips blotting paper into the stained notebook and presses it under a paperweight.
In the rainy season, Gu Heng in the shavings workshop sweeps damp shavings to the stove to dry.
Gu Heng brushes sawdust from the caliper jaws.
At dawn, Gu Heng in the instrument drying gallery checks the hygrometer.
Gu Heng hangs his raincoat on a gallery post and listens to rain on the glass roof.
In midsummer, Gu Heng opens the workshop skylight to drive out glue fumes.
Gu Heng checks the fish-glue pot temperature so it does not thicken too much.
When autumn wind rises, Gu Heng pulls cover cloths off the outdoor half-finished bodies.
Gu Heng tries a new arch code on a blank page of the luthier notebook.
On a frosty night, Gu Heng lights an oil lamp and checks the flashlight battery.
Gu Heng wraps the top plate in a blanket to prevent night cracking.
On a heavy-snow day, Gu Heng sweeps thin snow from the old workshop porch steps.
Gu Heng breathes on his hands and tightens the red cord on the soundpost blanks.
In early spring, Gu Heng trims the ivy on the porch.
Gu Heng oils all five calipers one by one.
Gu Heng posts a new schedule on the workshop wall.
Around the Dragon Boat Festival, Gu Heng smokes the wood store with mugwort to repel insects.
Gu Heng re-planes the end faces of the soundpost blanks.
Gu Heng paces alone in the instrument drying gallery, memorizing bass-bar positions.
After the rain stops, Gu Heng pushes open the workshop door and listens to eaves drip into an iron bucket.
Gu Heng swaps worn sandpaper for fresh.
Another dusk, Gu Heng sits by the spruce top plate listening to the radio.
Gu Heng gets up at night to refill the humidifier.
Gu Heng hangs fresh horsehair strings to straighten.
Gu Heng wipes the 'Hengsheng' porch plaque.
Gu Heng checks the instrument cart velvet for holes.
Gu Heng marks the f-hole position on the drawing.
Gu Heng wrings out a glue-stained rag and hangs it up.
On a full-moon night, Gu Heng leans on the gallery railing at the bodies, varnish silver in the light.
Gu Heng organizes the tool board so all caliper jaws face the same way.
Gu Heng writes a new season's luthier notes on the notebook flyleaf.
Gu Heng polishes both tuning forks.
Gu Heng listens to trial playing from the shopfront and keeps planing the top plate thinner.
Gu Heng glues a split wooden wedge back together.
Gu Heng stacks spare ribs in the workshop corner.
Gu Heng shuts doors and windows against sudden night humidity swings.
Another Qingming, Gu Heng places a bunch of wildflowers on the porch.
Gu Heng rolls the drawing into a tube and binds it with a rubber band.
Gu Heng taps a tuning fork; the tone rings clear.
Gu Heng sits silently in the workshop, listening to shavings fall for a long while.
Gu Heng cuts worn indigo cloth into rags for later use.
At daybreak, Gu Heng patrols the instrument drying gallery; the instrument cart stands at the gallery mouth.
Gu Heng crouches to check lubrication on the instrument cart axle.
Gu Heng walks to the bench corner; the same three soundpost blanks are still bound with red cord.
A red delivery tricycle（A red delivery tricycle, tin bed with no 'Gu' brand—unlike the wooden cart） passes outside the gallery, tin bed—not the Gu family's wooden cart.
Gu Heng stands in the instrument drying gallery and records the hygrometer reading.
Gu Heng hangs the damp velvet cloth on a gallery rack.
Gu Heng brushes shavings from his sleeve and looks back toward the workshop lights.
After Grain Rain, Gu Heng in the instrument drying gallery teaches a new apprentice to read tight vs loose grain.
Gu Heng drapes the dried cover cloths back over the bodies.
In summer heat, Gu Heng lays a damp cloth beside the fish-glue pot to cool it.
Gu Heng checks the instrument cart and moves the damp velvet to the upper layer.
On an autumn night, Gu Heng under the oil lamp mends loose pages of the luthier notebook.
Gu Heng sends all five calipers out for calibration in rotation.
At first snow, Gu Heng sweeps a narrow path at the old workshop porch threshold.
Gu Heng restacks spare pine boards neatly.
Gu Heng listens to a tuning fork's soft ring and keeps revising the schedule.
Gu Heng opens the gallery door to let a cross-breeze carry away glue smell.
Gu Heng hangs a rain awning on the porch.
Gu Heng puts chipped plane irons into an iron box.
Gu Heng dreams of the top plate cracking, wakes, and writes it in the notebook.
Gu Heng rinses calipers with clean water.
Gu Heng wipes the schedule clean and posts it again.
Gu Heng pulls weeds from mortar cracks in the gallery posts.
Gu Heng hangs calipers back on the tool board; the numbered tags have faded.
Gu Heng takes a last look at the spruce top plate crack before switching off the light.
Gu Heng folds the indigo headscarf the apprentice left in the workshop.
Gu Heng hears the shopfront lock at closing time and gets up to bolt the door.
Gu Heng dries gloves by the charcoal brazier.
Gu Heng moves the tuning forks aside to show the freshly repaired gallery eaves.
Gu Heng dries the humidity-test paper strips.
Gu Heng draws a thickness comparison on the notebook's last page.
Gu Heng murmurs tomorrow's top plate to join and steps out onto the porch.
Gu Heng pushes the instrument cart to the wall and clears shavings floor space.
Gu Heng hears a distant night watch drum and blows out the oil lamp.
Another rainy night, Gu Heng alone watches over the top plate until dawn.
Gu Heng trial-fits a newly arrived rosewood end block.
On a storm night, workshop humidity spikes; wood pops and creaks.
The bench trembles slightly in the shaking.
A faint snap—the spruce top plate（The same spruce top plate now cracked; fine splits along the grain, join lines misaligned） splits along the grain.
On the slope outside the gallery, the instrument cart loses control on wet ground.
The instrument cart（The instrument cart overturned on the slope; bed shattered, axle broken, reduced to wreckage） overturns; bed shattered, axle broken, utterly wrecked.
Gu Heng lunges to the bench and shields the cracking spruce top plate.
A neighbor arrives with a lantern; splintered wood lies outside the gallery.
The next day, Gu Heng stands in the shavings workshop staring at the cracked spruce top plate.
Gu Heng runs a finger along the crack, expression dim.
Gu Heng writes the instrument cart overturn date on a blank page of the luthier notebook.
An old photo of the instrument cart still hangs on the wall; Gu Heng stares a long while.
Gu Heng takes one of the five calipers from the tool board and recalibrates it.
The cracked spruce top plate still lies on the bench; join lines misaligned.
Gu Heng sets his wet boots by the door to drain.
Weeks later, Gu Heng brings in an inlay specialist to repair the spruce top plate.

Gu Heng takes a pine practice board（A pine practice board, coarser grain, no join lines—looks like the spruce top plate but cannot serve as a soundboard） from the rack to compare—coarser grain, no join lines.
The craftsman sets butterfly keys along the crack.
The crack closes; the spruce top plate（The spruce top plate crack closed with butterfly inlays; patch pieces clearly visible） is usable again, patch pieces clearly visible.
The repaired plate gleams in morning light; Gu Heng looks pleased at the butterfly keys.
Gu Heng re-planes the edges and trial-fits the bass bar.
Outside the gallery comes String merchant Old Qiao（String merchant Old Qiao, full beard, peg bag on his back, build like Gu Heng's but stockier）, peg bag on his back, build like Gu Heng's.

The Association supervisor（A lean Association supervisor, gray suit with chest badge, build somewhat like Gu Heng's but stiffer） arrives too, gray suit and chest badge, standing beside Gu Heng to talk.
The supervisor points at the red delivery tricycle and asks whether it belongs to the Hengsheng workshop.
The supervisor leaves; Gu Heng alone remains in the instrument drying gallery.
Old Qiao unloads a crate of strings and bows farewell.

At the shopfront comes girl Xiao Zheng（Shopfront girl Xiao Zheng, light-brown headscarf, at a glance somewhat like young A-Xian, shy eyes） in a light-brown headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young A-Xian.
Xiao Zheng tries wiping a bow; Gu Heng shakes his head—she is not A-Xian after all.
Xiao Zheng lowers her head shyly and tightens her headscarf.

Years later at dusk, Gu Heng（The same Gu Heng: apron torn, right hand bandaged, leaning on a wooden cane, glasses still on his nose） with bandaged right hand stands on his cane in the old workshop porch（Old workshop porch: gray-brick porch, lintel plaque 'Hengsheng' weathered, moss on the stone steps）.
Gu Heng looks up at the 'Hengsheng' plaque, gaze distant.
The two brass tuning forks have been moved to the porch for a trial ring; Gu Heng stops to listen.
Gu Heng presses his palm to the cool porch brick, as if saying goodbye.
Evening wind lifts a torn corner of his apron.
By day, adult A-Xian（A-Xian in his twenties, still in indigo headscarf, upright and steady） returns along the street and hurries toward the old workshop porch.
A-Xian reunites with cane-leaning Gu Heng under the porch; the two embrace.
In the inner room beside the couch, A-Xian holds Gu Heng's hand.
Gu Heng（Gu Heng has left the workshop; only his linen apron and glasses remain—he no longer appears）'s breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and retires from duty.
A-Xian folds Gu Heng's linen apron and sets it by the pillow.
Behind the workshop door Gu Heng's half-frame glasses still hang; A-Xian reaches up to touch them lightly.
On a porch post, A-Xian stands before the newly nailed memorial wood plaque（A cypress memorial wood plaque nailed to a porch post, carved with Gu Heng's name and the workshop founding year）.
A-Xian's fingertip traces Gu Heng's name carved on the memorial wood plaque.
A-Xian places a bunch of wildflowers beneath the plaque.
Disguised anew, A-Hui（Disguised anew, A-Hui still wears the cream-white neck scarf; hairpin swapped to black, expression deeper） comes from the shopfront and embraces A-Xian tightly under the porch.
A-Xian and A-Hui stand side by side on the porch—one calm-eyed, one deep in expression.
The two look at each other in silence, studying their similar faces.
A-Hui tightens her cream-white neck scarf; A-Xian still wears the indigo headscarf.
The camera returns years earlier—the youth measuring plate thickness in the instrument drying gallery appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the workshop, a tight-grain board shows its grain for the first time.
Flash back to the shopfront that year—a figure in cream-white neck scarf and ebony temple hairpin flashes past.
Before the eyes rises that row of five vernier measures on the tool board again.
Back to the long gallery at first meeting—half-finished bodies hanging as before.
The scene of two brass tuning forks ringing softly under the gallery eaves appears again.
A-Xian opens the glue-stained luthier notebook again and walks into the shavings workshop.
On the bench corner, the same three soundpost blanks are still bound with red cord.
A-Xian takes the butterfly-patched spruce top plate and planes it open for cutting again.
Fresh green pushes through the porch stone cracks again.
A-Xian tightens his indigo headscarf; workshop lamps glow once more.
